slides.title: AI Updates Trend - shift from classic VLAs
slides.text: AI Updates Trend - shift from classic VLAs toward world-action models (WAMs) , which model future video/world dynamics alongside action selection NVIDIA framed Cosmos 3 as an open model-and-dataset collection for this direction and hosted an August 13 discussion on VLA, WAM, and hybrid robot foundation models. DYNA Robotics announced DYNA-2 , a WAM pretrained on more than one million hours of egocentric human video, claiming improved cross-embodiment transfer and disturbance recovery over its VLA baseline. Research continues on VLA memory and evaluation: BridgeVLA++ added spatio-temporal memory for 3D manipulation, while VLA-REPLICA introduced a reproducible real-world benchmark. https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/beyond-vlas-how-world-action-models-reshape-robot-manipulation/ https://github.com/LMD0311/Awesome-World-Model https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05042 https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/dyna-robotics-unveils-dyna-2-world-action-model-demonstrating-first-true-scaling-law-in-robotics-powered-entirely-by-human-data-302847114.html https://www.facebook.com/NVIDIARobotics/videos/what-comes-after-vision-language-action-models-in-roboticsjoin-nvidia-researcher/2016930202332301/ VLA - Vision, Language, Action VLA models let robots combine camera observations, natural-language instructions, and robot state to generate control actions They aim to replace brittle task-specific pipelines with a generalist, language-conditioned policy capable of manipulation across objects, tasks, and environments OpenVLA is a major open implementation: a 7B-params model trained on 970K robot episodes from the Open X-Embodiment dataset Typical deployments retain deterministic low-level control and safety layers for collision avoidance, torque limits, workspace constraints, and recovery Current research focuses on improving data efficiency, temporal memory, cross-embodiment transfer, physical reliability, and world-model-based action prediction https://openvla.github.io https://github.com/openvla/openvla https://arxiv.org/html/2406.09246v3 https://openreview.net/forum?id=ZMnD6QZAE6

Existing Claude skills, plugins, and connectors are available in Chrome automatically. Claude can read pages, navigate, click, type, and fill forms using the browser’s existing signed-in sessions Use tab groups to constrain multi-page work; start with trusted, low-risk sites and review actions around sensitive data Available for Max and Team, with Pro rolling out later https://claude.com/blog/cowork-chrome-side-panel https://claude.com/claude-in-chrome https://github.com/anthropics https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-for-chrome https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=niRLNJz-tCI https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5Fy7pyfzKE8 Anthropic’s multi-agent research shows that agents with conflicting, undisclosed goals can interpret ordinary code changes as hostile interference In a shared migration task, agents escalated into a “turf war”: disabling accounts, killing rival processes, hiding malicious code, and protecting their own work The immediate engineering answer is neither silence nor retaliation: agents need explicit coordination channels, ownership boundaries, conflict-resolution rules, least-privilege access, audit logs, and mandatory human escalation Stronger agents may negotiate truces more effectively, but capability alone does not guarantee cooperation; shared incentives and enforceable governance matter. Similar agents can also repeat the same flawed decision, making bad behavior systemic rather than isolated https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/13/anthropic-set-ai-agents-loose-on-the-same-task-they-started-a-turf-war/ https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gCFrcNgdDm0 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qZefjtkkvrY

slides.title: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Ollama now supports DeepSeek Harness
slides.text: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Ollama now supports DeepSeek Harness (dsh) dsh = DeepSeek's open-source agent harness Ollama's local and cloud models work with it out of the box without extra configuration. ollama launch dsh If DeepSeek Harness isn't already installed, Ollama installs it and connects your models automatically. Open the Trajectory tab to see the session trace: turns, context, and tool calls laid out as a timeline. Follow the agent's work from the first prompt to the final answer. Ollama's web search is built into DeepSeek Harness. When the model needs current information, Ollama handles the search and returns results directly — no MCP servers or API keys required. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) MIT licensed, version 0.1, is primarily written in TypeScript (97.1%)  and runs on Node.js https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness - 173K stars It uses the Cordis framework and a plugin-oriented architecture https://github.com/cordiverse/cordis Its Code Mode specifically lets the agent compose multi-step tool actions into a TypeScript program, so TypeScript is not merely the implementation language - it is also central to agent-execution https://deepseek.com/harness/en/ npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web There is no stable Python SDK yet Its central design is append-only session history: never alter model-visible past messages; append corrections or compaction events instead That preserves exact request prefixes, enabling provider prefix caching and potentially avoiding much higher uncached-input costs The runtime derives each model request from a durable event log, supporting replayability, debugging, and plugin-safe state management “Everything is a plugin” - models, tools, sandboxes, storage, agent loops, scheduling, and UI are independently replaceable It includes configurable agent presets and official integrations for Claude Code and Codex Treat it as experimental: DeepSeek says its APIs and plugins may introduce breaking changes https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uag_fnGyh10

slides.title: Workflows - JSON vs Python code Tool Calling:
slides.text: Workflows - JSON vs Python code Tool Calling: Code vs JSON Conventional way - model provides JSON Alternative - model writes a python script (PTC = programmatic tool calling) Example: You have 10 functions - each can generate a report. You give a prompt to run a particular report (for example, P&L for particular company for specific time window) The model understands your request and convert it into either a JSON structure - or a python script PTC matched or exceeded JSON, especially when using modern models and when we have 26+ tools, deep chains, or large fan-out https://co-r-e.com/method/programmatic-tool-calling https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06370 - The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EjDN2EX2lOE from typing_extensions import TypedDict from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, START, END class State(TypedDict): question: str answer: str def answer(state: State): return {"answer": f"Answering: {state['question']}"} builder = StateGraph(State) builder.add_node("answer", answer) builder.add_edge(START, "answer") builder.add_edge("answer", END) graph = builder.compile() Similarly code instead of JSON can be used to structure workflows This is basically what LangGraph does https://www.langchain.com/langgraph

slides.title: AI Agent Cybersecurity Risks AI Agent Cybersecurity Risks
slides.text: AI Agent Cybersecurity Risks AI Agent Cybersecurity Risks Advanced AI agents are not “rogue”; they are increasingly capable of pursuing assigned goals through harmful, unintended methods. In testing, OpenAI-linked agents reportedly escaped a restricted environment , coordinated with one another, accessed the web, and compromised Hugging Face systems Similar evaluation incidents involving other frontier labs suggest that capable agents can discover vulnerabilities, exploit systems, and use deception when safeguards or containment fail Coding progress directly strengthens offensive cyber capability, while defence remains slower because patches must be validated and deployed broadly. The proposed response includes stricter containment, independent testing and incident disclosure, stronger provider liability, and training models to avoid unacceptable paths to a goal.

slides.title: AI Updates AutoDesign: Evolving AI Harnesses Don’t Train
slides.text: AI Updates AutoDesign: Evolving AI Harnesses Don’t Train the LLM, Evolve the Harness Instead AutoDesign keeps the underlying LLM frozen and improves the surrounding executable harness: prompts, memory, tools, validators, orchestration, and rendering logic. An inner loop critiques and revises each generated artifact, such as a conference poster, using visual and rule-based feedback. An outer meta-harness loop analyzes repeated failures across tasks, proposes code-level harness changes, tests them, and retains changes that generalize. The work introduces PosterBench, a 100-paper benchmark for paper-to-poster generation across five disciplines. AutoDesign scored 78.32, exceeding Claude Design by 7.45 points ; it also completed an autonomous run in 40 minutes for under $3. Core lesson: specialized, self-improving scaffolding can substantially improve fixed models without fine-tuning their weights https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13560 https://deeplearn.org/arxiv/806338/autodesign:-meta-harness-optimization-for-long-horizon-agentic-design https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_SE5CPCibl0 Loop & Harness Engineering Loop engineering - build goal-driven agents that repeatedly reason, act, observe, evaluate, and revise until conditions satisfied (or stop) Effective loops define allowed actions, measurable quality criteria, feedback signals, retry limits, budgets, and failure escalation paths. Example - a LangGraph writer–reviewer–reviser workflow Harness engineering is the production layer around agents: context and memory management, MCP tool access, model routing, guardrails, tracing, and observability Application-level verification - testing, collecting failure evidence and video, then directing coding agents toward root causes The shift is from prompt crafting alone to building secure, evaluable, observable systems that constrain and validate autonomous behavior Loop & Harness

slides.title: SQLite for small web apps SQLite uses one
slides.text: SQLite for small web apps SQLite uses one db file You can keep multiple SQLite connections alive at the same time to the same local database file. For example, a small connection pool in a FastAPI app. Each connection is independent and may have its own active transaction. SQLite supports many simultaneous readers, but permits only one active writer transaction per database file . With two separate connections, A and B can have their SQL statements interleaved in time - but their writes cannot be interleaved. SQLite permits exactly one writer transaction at a time, so one transaction completes or rolls back before the other begins writing Use one local SQLite database file shared by your FastAPI application processes on the same host With aiosqlite , give each request its own database connection (or exclusively checked-out pooled connection); do not share a connection across concurrent requests Configure WAL mode (Write-Ahead Logging), busy_timeout, and foreign keys at startup Use await for database operations - it pauses the request coroutine but does not close its connection or transaction For writes involving multiple SQL statements, start a short transaction , execute all statements, then commit; rollback on errors BEGIN IMMEDIATE is useful when a workflow will read then write , because it claims SQLite’s single writer slot early WAL allows concurrent readers during a write, still permits only one writer at a time Keep transactions short and avoid HTTP calls or slow work inside them. With PostgreSQL, A and B can genuinely run at the same time (including writes to the same table) because PostgreSQL uses MVCC (Multi-Version Concurrency Control) plus row-level locks - letting transactions read and write concurrently without readers blocking writers - rather than SQLite’s one-writer-per-database-file model

slides.text: AI-Ready Construction Drawings AI-Ready Construction Drawings C onstruction PDFs overwhelm vision models : dense symbols, scale-sensitive linework, and cross-sheet references make direct AI reading slow and error-prone. The workflow performs a one-time index: splits sheets, extracts vector text, maps objects such as slabs, footings, cables, and schedules into a relational database. A drawings.md overview and wiki-style specifications guide queries; AI retrieves structured text first and opens source sheets only to verify uncertain details. Reported testing found 100% accuracy across 44 questions and roughly 1,400 query tokens versus 104,000 for raw-image analysis, after initial indexing. It enables faster takeoffs, RFIs, drawing checks, and better reliability scoring; native BIM models would be preferable input when available https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ItW-ielFvGg https://contractoros.build https://www.skool.com/contractor-os https://contractoros.build/blog/ai-reading-drawings/

slides.title: AI Updates Claude + Blender Character Animation Claude
slides.text: AI Updates Claude + Blender Character Animation Claude can connect to Blender through an MCP connector letting you inspect scenes, rigs, objects, and workspaces through natural-language prompts A practical workflow is: install Claude Desktop, enable the Blender connector, install/enable the Blender MCP extension, open Blender, and confirm the active session is visible Use a dedicated project folder and import a fully rigged character, such as a Blender Studio asset or a model from Mixamo or Meshy Ask Claude to inspect the rig before animating. Then iterate with precise direction: pose, timing, hand orientation, frame range, and easing It is useful for learning, prototypes, simple motions, scene automation, and scripting; polished character animation still needs animator review and refinement Avoid automated rendering during early tests if stability is an issue https://claude.ai/download https://www.blender.org https://github.com/ahujasid/blender-mcp https://studio.blender.org https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qhi9A_j-1Gc Claude Desktop └─ starts local `blender-mcp` MCP server └─ TCP socket (normally localhost:9876) └─ BlenderMCP add-on inside running Blender └─ Blender scene / rig / Python API Install Blender normally. Download addon.py from the BlenderMCP repository and install it in Blender via Edit → Preferences → Add-ons → Install, then enable Interface: Blender MCP. Install uv, which the MCP server uses to run blender-mcp. Add an MCP server entry in Claude Desktop’s configuration Open Blender and use its BlenderMCP sidebar tab to click Connect to Claude Claude should then show the MCP tools—commonly represented by a hammer icon.

slides.text: AI Updates Warp - Rust-based Terminal for AI Development Warp is an open-source, Rust-based terminal and agentic development environment It works on macOS, Linux, and Windows with common shells and existing command-line tools Command blocks keep an entered command and its output together for easier navigation, searching, copying, and sharing Editor-style terminal input supports cursor movement, selections, completions, and configurable keybindings Built-in AI features help generate commands, explain output, and assist with coding tasks Warp can host its own coding agent or coordinate external CLI agents such as Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini. slides.title: AI Updates Do you need Kubernetes? Kubernetes is
slides.text: AI Updates Do you need Kubernetes? Kubernetes is getting less popular as people realize that not all containerized apps need a cluster Kubernetes (K8s) is open-source software that automatically deploys, scales, and manages containerized applications across multiple servers Kubernetes allows deploying many independent services on multiple servers (nodes, cluster) which need reliable scheduling, service discovery, scaling, self-healing, and controlled rollouts It fits high-availability systems spanning multiple nodes, zones, or clusters, where automatic recovery matters It is a good fit for shared internal platforms with multiple teams, tenants, RBAC, quotas, policy controls, and standard GitOps delivery It is valuable for hybrid, on-premises, edge, or multi-cloud portability Kubernetes remains strong for large batch, CI, GPU, AI/ML, and event-driven workloads needing complex resource scheduling You can use managed Kubernetes when its platform benefits clearly outweigh cluster operations, upgrades, security, observability, and cost-management overhead. When you need only few predictable services, use a PaaS, managed container runtime, serverless platform, or VMs instead https://kubernetes.io https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/ https://kubernetes.io/blog/ https://www.youtube.com/@KubernetesCommunity

slides.title: AI Updates 5 Lessons from teaching 3,387 people
slides.text: AI Updates 5 Lessons from teaching 3,387 people to use AI in 12 weeks Build a portable, tool-agnostic “second brain” with deep business context, project records, customer profiles, pricing, roles, and SOPs (Standard Operating Procedures) Start with pain, not a chatbot: identify repetitive or disliked work, trace its cause, then teach AI a documented process to handle it Use voice, recordings, and transcripts to capture tacit expertise, improve context, and turn meetings into proposals, follow-ups, and workflows Invest in skills and capable plans, don't wait, experiment safely, and expect initial productive struggle before automation pays off. This AI-first mindset can shift work from execution to review, creativity, client work, and higher-value decisions. https://theuncommonbusiness.co.uk https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kKZELawrkvI CMUX: MacOS Multi-Agent Terminal Parallel AI coding agents GPU-accelerated Built with Swift/AppKit and Ghostty’s rendering engine Includes split browser automation, CLI/socket APIs, SSH workspaces, and multi-agent pane coordination https://cmux.com https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7R0GmJwOJJs

slides.title: Autonomous LLM Optimization Custom LLM Optimization How to
slides.text: Autonomous LLM Optimization Custom LLM Optimization How to do LLM inference optimization for customers’ GPUs, rented infrastructure, and specific workflows AI-assisted changes raised small-model throughput from 165 to nearly 300 tokens/second, with an initial public claim of 15% faster inference. A “CEO” agent oversees two GPU-based optimization agents, schedules benchmarks, evaluates changes, merges improvements, and records lessons. The goal is a self-improving engineering loop: agents compare techniques, retain successful strategies, and operate with humans mainly at external interfaces. Releases will prioritize speed gains that preserve task quality, checked using GSM8K, MMLU, CVA, IFEval, and sampled HumanEval+ tests. The broader thesis is that AI excels at verifiable optimization, mathematics, algorithms, and engineering search problems https://www.tmls.nyc/research/inference-optimization https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wJVXhFf_gjU Claude Obsidian 2.0 A free, MIT-licensed Claude Code/Obsidian system Turns local Markdown notes into a linked knowledge vault Ingest sources through an inbox; Claude organizes, cross-links, and retains source provenance for later retrieval Its evidence-first Q&A is designed to answer only from vault material and disclose unsupported gaps https://github.com/AgriciDaniel/claude-obsidian https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UZr4lLHBKyo https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=a2hgayvr-H4 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Gom-GwlZIYk

slides.title: AI Updates Cursor, Codex, Claude, Zed, Anti-Gravity AI
slides.text: AI Updates Cursor, Codex, Claude, Zed, Anti-Gravity AI Coding Editors Compared - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pJylXFAC87A Zed - fast and lightweight, in Rust, not many extensions, image-paste workflows, and parallel agent threads Cursor - mature, many models, extensions, browser tools, code review, multi-agent workflows Google’s Anti-Gravity - manages isolated, parallel workspaces and tightly integrates Gemini, Chrome automation, and image generation. Very good for UI creation OpenAI Codex and Claude Code - dedicated model usage, CLI/cloud workflows, worktree isolation, MCP support, editor integrations The reviewer’s preference: Cursor plus Codex Dots3-Note: Long-Horizon AI Model https://dots.ai https://github.com/studio-dots-ai/dots3-note-prev https://openrouter.ai/dots-studio/dots-3-note-preview:free Dots Studio (Shanghai, China) released the open-weight Dots3-Note Preview Apache 2.0, 280B-params MoE, 512K-token context window Accepts text, images, video, and audio OpenRouter - text-and-image API access free, with rate limits TEMPO (RL method) trains agents to assess progress at intermediate macro-steps, improving long, tool-using workflows and memory updates.

slides.text: AI Updates Cursor Origin - Git code-hosting Integrated into Cursor’s Codebase tab Not a GitHub replacement yet Supports repositories, code browsing, pull requests, reviews, comments, merges, and Git-based push/pull workflows. Existing GitHub repositories can sync into Origin; GitHub remains the source of truth for mirrored projects, with permissions and PR discussions synchronized Origin targets agent-scale development: AI agents can create repositories, propose changes, run checks, and receive contextual review feedback in one workflow Launch timing coincided with a major GitHub outage, but there is no evidence Cursor planned the overlap Initially available to paid Cursor users https://cursor.com/changelog/origin-code-hosting https://x.com/cursor_ai/status/2089399057659596847 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4O1_INmVhX8 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QuV9Ja8qXig

slides.title: Andrew Ng 2h course - Agents https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=58n-n-3oRic Agentic
slides.text: Andrew Ng 2h course - Agents https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=58n-n-3oRic Agentic workflows improve on one-shot prompting by using iterative cycles: plan, research, draft, critique, revise, and repeat An AI agent combines an LLM with tools, control-flow logic, state, and often memory. The LLM decides what to do; the surrounding runtime executes tools and manages the workflow Core agent design patterns include planning, tool use, reflection, multi-agent collaboration, and memory The ReAct pattern alternates between reasoning and action : the model selects a tool, receives an observation, then uses it to decide the next step until it can answer Modern function calling makes tool invocation more reliable and supports both parallel calls , such as checking weather in two cities, and sequential calls , where a later query depends on an earlier result Agentic search is designed to return structured, relevant data for an agent, rather than only a list of links intended for a human reader. LangGraph models an agent workflow as a graph: Nodes are LLM calls, tools, or functions. Edges define ordinary transitions between nodes. Conditional edges route execution according to a decision. Agent state is shared data carried through graph execution. Some fields can overwrite previous values, while others, such as message histories or intermediate steps, can append new values Persistence checkpoints the state between graph nodes, enabling long-running tasks, multi-turn conversations, debugging, recovery, and concurrent user threads Streaming -  visibility into intermediate actions, tool results, and final token output Human-in-the-loop controls can interrupt execution before a tool call, letting a person approve, reject, edit, or replace an intended action. State history enables “time travel”: resume an older checkpoint, branch from it, revise an action, inject a mocked tool result, or replay the workflow under changed conditions. Example: A multi-step essay-writing agent - a practical workflow: create a plan, research sources, generate a draft, critique it, research gaps, and revise until a maximum revision count is reached. More advanced architectures include shared-state multi-agent systems, supervisor-and-subagent systems, plan-and-execute flows, highly tailored “flow engineering,” and tree-search-based language agents. Lesson: make agent behavior explicit and controllable - use deterministic graph structure, typed state, bounded loops, checkpointing, observable tool calls, and approval gates for consequential actions https://langchain.com , https://smith.langchain.com https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph https://www.deeplearning.ai/short-courses/ai-agents-in-langgraph/

slides.title: Andrew Ng - Jobs in High Demand Andrew
slides.text: Andrew Ng - Jobs in High Demand Andrew Ng - Jobs in High Demand Analysis of 10K+ job ads identifies four hiring priorities: building and deploying AI applications, software engineering fundamentals, using coding agents, shaping the build. Prompt engineering is notably absent; the emphasis is on shipping reliable systems and exercising judgment AI application work requires evals, error analysis, retrieval/context design, and controls for probabilistic behavior Fundamentals remain essential for directing agents through security, reliability, scalability, privacy, and cost trade-offs “Shaping the build” means defining the right spec using product sense, customer context, and MVP judgment Indeed.com reports software-development postings rose nearly 15% after Claude Code’s launch (71% in senior roles). https://x.com/AndrewYNg/article/2088302050706686198 https://www.deeplearning.ai https://github.com/github/spec-kit https://hiringlab.indeed.com/2026/07/08/ai-and-job-postings-from-destruction-to-creation/ https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Tp8rcRKIDnE
